name: J.C. Wessel
strengths: Wessel tracks the underthrown ball over his shoulder, snags it, and breaks the first tackle up the sideline.
Wessel explodes out of a three-point stance and flattens the edge on the inline run block.
Wessel catches the crosser in stride, takes a big hit at the catch point, and keeps the ball.
Wessel flexes into the slot and still accelerates down the seam with that 6-6 frame.
weaknesses: Wessel wins with size and contact balance more than suddenness — route twitch and pad level are the next step.
comparison: Wessel comps to Kyle Pitts — 6-6 / 246 long Y / flexed tight end who can track the seam ball and still put his hands on an edge.
projection: Wessel projects as a Year 1 developmental Y, then a Year 2 rotation tight end, with Year 3 starter upside if the inline block stays nasty at Bolles.
schemeFit: Wessel fits a traditional Y who can flex — seam threat and drive-block TE, not a gadget H-back.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-09-23 from Frederica Academy sophomore reel (embed 23224172 / 69025c880d2241dbb094580d). Wessel is now at The Bolles School. Comp height-matched within ~1 inch — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: J.C. Wessel is a 2028 TE · listed 6-6.5 / 227 · The Bolles School (Jacksonville, FL) · sophomore tape is Frederica Academy · expected Ole Miss weekend in the Swamp.
angle: Lead with the catch-and-break and the pancake edge block; Wessel is a true Y.
insiderNotes: Wessel is a 6-6.5 / 227 Y. On the Frederica sophomore sit he tracks the underthrown ball, flattens the edge inline, and holds the crosser through a big hit. He is at Bolles now.
